subject: Acme Payments - vulnerability evidence, cadence & signed attestation
messages:
From: David Choe <david.choe@acme-payments.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-payments.com, Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@thirdparty-audit.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: VM evidence + CVE remediation SLA attestation

Vanessa / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our quarterly SIG review we need a concise evidence bundle that covers:
- scan cadence (last 12 months) and scheduled recurrence policy
- SLA for critical/high CVE remediation (mean/median times to remediation and escalation paths)
- confirmation that prefix/KV-cache and runtime hotfixes are included in the remediation scope
- a signed attestation we can share with our internal audit + external assessors (Lara is copied)

Could you provide the evidence packet and signed attestation by EOD Friday, Sep 2nd? If you need a different deadline, let us know. Also flag any temporary exceptions we should track in the SIG matrix.

Appreciate it —
David
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments
[attachment: request-form_acme_q3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: David Choe <david.choe@acme-payments.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 16:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + CVE remediation SLA attestation

David — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it. High level plan:
1) I will assemble the scan cadence CSV (monthly authenticated scans + weekly dependency scans) and an executive summary of the last 12 months.
2) Marcus will provide the CVE SLA metrics and escalation flow (we record detection -> triage -> owner assignment -> patch -> verification).
3) Kimberly will prepare the signed attestation PDF and include the control owner signature block.

We can deliver an evidence bundle (CSV + summary + attestation) by Sep 2 EOD. If you need an earlier handoff for the auditors, we can send an interim summary tomorrow.

Attachments I will include in the final packet: redwood-vm-scan-schedule.csv, scan-horizon-mapping.xlsx, redwood-cve-attestation-draft.pdf.

Quick question: do you need remediation median times broken out by host/service vs. containerized model endpoints? We can provide both but want to confirm which is preferable for Acme's SIG template.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
[attachment: placeholder_evidence_index.txt (TXT, 1KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: David Choe <david.choe@acme-payments.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + CVE remediation SLA attestation

David / Vanessa — adding the technical detail requested. Summary of our standard cadence and SLA measurements: 

- Scanning cadence: authenticated host scans (monthly), unauthenticated perimeter scans (weekly), dependency vulnerability scans (weekly), container image scans (on-build + weekly registry sweep).
- Coverage: all hosted inference clusters + orchestration nodes; private deployments are validated per-customer with exported scan manifests.
- SLA definitions (current production policy):
  * Critical (CVSS >=9.0 or exploitable RCE with proof): target remediation time 72 hours to mitigation/fix, 7 days to full verification.
  * High (CVSS 7.0-8.9): target remediation time 14 days.
  * Medium/Low: prioritized backlog with normal release cadence.
- Measurement: timestamps we include are detection_time, ticket_creation, owner_assign, patch_deployed, verification_complete. We compute median & 95th percentile over the rolling 12 months.

We will attach a small sample CSV with the last 12 months' critical/high events and anonymized IDs. For Acme's SIG template, we recommend the host/service breakouts — that gives auditors the most utility.

Marcus
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: sample_cve_timeline.csv (CSV, 48KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Choe <david.choe@acme-payments.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 11:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + CVE remediation SLA attestation

David / team — attaching the signed attestation and the final evidence index. The attestation confirms:
- Monthly authenticated scans + weekly dependency sweeps have been executed for the last 12 months (exceptions documented in the index).
- SLA targets for Critical/High as described by Marcus have been observed and measured; we include median and 95th percentile values in the CSV.
- When customers are on Redwood Private we provide a validated scan manifest export; for Dedicated/Hosted the scans are performed centrally but per-account exports can be generated on request.

Attachments: redwood-cve-attestation-signed.pdf (signed by Kim Park, Head of Security Compliance), redwood-vm-scan-schedule.csv, scan-horizon-mapping.xlsx

If Acme needs a DocuSign route, I can send the attestation to our DocuSign flow and share the link.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security Compliance, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-cve-attestation-signed.pdf (PDF, 18KB); redwood-vm-scan-schedule.csv (CSV, 56KB); scan-horizon-mapping.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)]

Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + CVE remediation SLA attestation

Thanks — bundle received and this looks good. Lara: I'll attach Kim's signed PDF to our SIG evidence packet. A couple of follow-ups: 
- Can Redwood confirm whether the 95th percentile remediation time for Criticals included one outlier incident in May (ticket id anonymized in the CSV)? If so, can you supply the short incident note or mark it as exception in the attestation index?
- Please send the DocuSign link for our records (we need an audit trail).

If you can add the exception note (one paragraph) and the DocuSign link by EOD, we'll mark this item as closed on our side.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
David
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments
